extraction_notes.note: The theorem environment closes before its enumerated conclusions, which sit in a separate {\it enumerate} block. TP2 keeps the environment span; the two items are emitted as part-claims outside it, each with a uses edge into TP2, and the proof has proves edges to all three.

The numbered equation (2.1) is named the magnetostatic Maxwell's equation, so it was retyped as an external theorem per the named-equation rule. It is a physical law rather than a mathematical theorem.

These numbered equations are standalone optimization formulations (Frame-Int, Frame-Diff), so they were retyped as problem. The analogous formulations in prose (Tikhonov, SMV, HIRE) are problem nodes that contain their numbered equation.
The sentence both introduces the discrete Laplacian and asserts the discrete harmonic property. It is kept as one heuristic claim rather than a definition.
An align* with a \label is reported as an environment fact although it is unnumbered. It was emitted as an equation node because the rules say every fact gets its node.
The standard QSM pipeline lists four steps but describes only three in its sentence. Those three are the algorithm steps; dipole inversion is the separate problem node ProbP1 in the next paragraph.

Left out: the experimental setup (data simulation, parameter choices, stopping criterion), the figure and table content, and the discursive motivation paragraphs comparing artifact types. Only the headline experimental conclusions are kept, as numerical claims.
